note: Placed pieces (docs 09, docs/future/10; src/world/pieces): objects that rest on the ground rather than being part of it. The first is the loose stone, the naturalist's reward at six finds (naturalist.json). cap: how many loose stones an island may hold; at the cap the Loose stone mode says so calmly and sets no more. sizeM: a stone's length in meters [min, max], picked by its seed. sink: the share of a stone's height set into the ground, so it sits rather than rests. tapM and tapPerM: how near a tap must be to pick a stone (plus this much per meter of camera distance; never less than about half the stone's length). arrive: when the reward is given, count stones come by themselves on grounds (painted grass or soil) between nearM [min, max] meters from fresh water (a pond or stream, never the sea or a damp hollow), never in water, on ground no steeper than maxSlope (rise over run across a meter), at least spacingM apart; placed from the world seed, so live play and catch-up give the same stones. tip: a tap on a stone lifts its near edge by tipDeg over tipS seconds (pivoting on the far edge, so you see underneath), holds for holdS, then settles back over settleS. shape: the stones are baked from blended ellipsoids (src/world/creatures/body-bake.js): count shapes, seeded from seed; widthShare and heightShare [min, max] of the length; lobes extra lumps blended in by blendM; cellM the bake grid; albedo the dry rock and underside the damp, soil-stained underneath (both linear and physical: the palette paints at tonemap, docs/05); speckle how much the rock's tone wanders over its face. damp: the dark patch the stone leaves on the ground, as a share of its footprint (scale), with its albedo at the middle and edge (linear). look: the creature pass's sheen (wetSpecular) and the body length its contact shadow is sized from (scaleReal, in mesh units: a stone's mesh is 1 long). words: the Loose stone mode's calm lines (full at the cap, water when a tap lands in water).

words.full: The island holds all the loose stones it can for now. Remove one to set it somewhere else.
words.water: A loose stone sits on land. Tap the ground.
